Focus on mobile-first but ensure excellent desktop layouts. Use Next.js 16 (app router) + TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 and shadcn/ui for components. Do not implement any CMS, backend, or dynamic data sources — produce a static site with clearly labeled placeholder data files (JSON or TS) that will later be wired to a custom CMS. The public site must remain fully static for now.Design goals- Tone: Minimalist, modern aesthetic, clear, and highly scannable.- Special layout element: include multiple bento grids in the visual design (at least two distinct bento-style grids — e.g., Projects and Work Highlights or Projects and Side Projects/Case Studies). Bento grids should feel modular and crafted (tiles of mixed aspect ratios, consistent gutters, intentional negative space).- Emphasize whitespace, strong typographic hierarchy, and modest micro-animations (fade/scale/slide) only where they add clarity.- Accessibility: semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, ARIA for complex widgets, and WCAG color contrast \u003e= AA.Technical constraints \u0026 stack specifics- Next.js 16 using the app/ directory and server components where appropriate. Use TypeScript everywhere.- Styling: Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first); include a small global CSS file (e.g., &#96;styles/globals.css&#96;) that &#96;@import \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; and declares your &#96;@theme&#96; tokens. If needed, include a short note showing where to load a legacy &#96;tailwind.config.js&#96; via &#96;@config&#96;.- UI primitives: shadcn/ui components (Avatar, Card, Button, Tabs, Badge, Toast/ToastProvider, Dialog for contact modal, etc.). Use those for consistent styling.- Images: use &#96;next/image&#96; for optimization. Provide a circular/rounded slot for a face photo with an accessible &#96;alt&#96; and a fallback SVG.- Project data / experiences / employment mode: create a &#96;data/&#96; or &#96;lib/seed.ts&#96; file with typed placeholders (array of projects, experiences, boolean &#96;isEmployed&#96;) — do not implement toggling logic; just include the static value and render UI accordingly.- File structure: produce a clean, modular structure (&#96;app/&#96;, &#96;components/&#96;, &#96;lib/&#96; or &#96;data/&#96;, &#96;styles/&#96;, &#96;public/&#96;).- Types: supply clear TypeScript interfaces for Project, Experience, SocialLink, etc.Layout \u0026 sections (mobile-first)1. Top meta \u0026 SEO   - Proper &#96;\u003chead\u003e&#96; metadata: title, description, og:image placeholder, twitter card.2. Hero (above the fold)   - Small circular face photo slot (prominent but balanced).   - Name (H1), Role (H2), 1–2 line punchy tagline/bio.   - Primary CTAs: “View projects” (scroll to Projects) and “Download resume” (link to static PDF in /public).   - A compact status indicator near the name: &#96;Employed&#96; / &#96;Open to work&#96; (rendered from the static boolean).3. Key skills strip   - Horizontal, scrollable chips on mobile; grouped badges on desktop.4. Bento Grid — Projects   - A responsive, masonry-like bento grid of project cards (mixed tile sizes: 1x1, 2x1, 1x2).   - Each tile: project image, short title, 1-line tagline, tech badges on hover, and a subtle CTA “Case study” / “Repo”.   - On mobile show 2 columns; tablet 3; desktop 4–6 depending on width. Maintain consistent gutter (16px/1rem).5. Bento Grid — Work Highlights / Case Studies   - Second distinct bento grid used to highlight 3–6 big wins or case studies with larger hero tiles and short metrics.6. About / Bio   - Short narrative, timeline style mini-education or who-I-am box. Include a “Download CV” and a subtle photo repeat.7. Experience (static)   - Chronological cards — company, role, dates, 2–3 bullets. Keep compact for mobile; detail on desktop.8. Mini demo / code sample   - A small stylized code card (use JetBrains Mono or system-mono) showing a 6–10 line code snippet and a button to view repo.9. Contact \u0026 social   - Email contact CTA, social icons (GitHub, LinkedIn, X, Mastodon if desired). Include a modal contact form (static — no backend).10. Footer    - Copyright, small nav, link to resume and privacy.Design system \u0026 visual details- Colors: minimal neutral palette + one accent.  - Example palette (use these hex suggestions but feel free to adapt minimally): Background &#96;#0F1724&#96; or off-white &#96;#F8FAFC&#96; (light/dark support), Surface &#96;#FFFFFF&#96;/&#96;#0B1220&#96;, Accent &#96;#6C5CE7&#96; or &#96;#7C3AED&#96;, Muted text &#96;#64748B&#96;.  - Provide both light and dark themes toggle (persisted to localStorage) but default to system preference.- Typography:  - Sans variable for UI (Inter or Inter var) and monospace for code (JetBrains Mono).  - Large, readable sizes: mobile H1 ≈ 28–32px, desktop H1 ≈ 44–56px.- Spacing \u0026 grid:  - Mobile-first spacing scale, consistent container widths and max-width for desktop (e.g., &#96;max-w-6xl&#96;).  - Bento tile sizing semantics: define utility classes or a &#96;tile&#96; component that accepts &#96;cols&#96; and &#96;rows&#96;.- Components:  - Reusable &#96;Avatar&#96;, &#96;ClippedImage&#96;, &#96;BentoGrid&#96; (configurable), &#96;ProjectCard&#96;, &#96;ExperienceCard&#96;, &#96;SkillChips&#96;, &#96;Navbar&#96; (minimal), &#96;Footer&#96;.  - &#96;BentoGrid&#96; should accept tile definitions so a future CMS can drive layout.- Micro-interactions:  - Subtle hover elevation (translateY -4px, shadow) and focus rings for accessibility. Use &#96;prefers-reduced-motion&#96;.- Performance \u0026 best practices:  - Optimize images, use lazy loading, prefetch critical resources, static rendering (no client-only heavy JS).  - Semantic HTML and ARIA attributes for interactive components.IMPORTANT TAILWIND v4 NOTES (follow these rules)- Use Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first). Import Tailwind in your CSS with &#96;@import \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96;, not &#96;@tailwind&#96; directives.- Define design tokens, custom utilities, and settings in CSS using the new &#96;@theme&#96; at-rule and related directives (so there is no default &#96;tailwind.config.ts&#96;). If you intentionally want to keep a legacy JS/TS configuration, load it explicitly from CSS using &#96;@config \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"./tailwind.config.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; (this is allowed for backward compatibility), but prefer CSS-first. - Use &#96;@tailwindcss/postcss&#96; for PostCSS setups or &#96;@tailwindcss/vite&#96; when using Vite/Next dev tooling. Use &#96;@tailwindcss/cli&#96; for CLI commands. - Keep compatibility with Tailwind v4 features: automatic content detection, CSS theme variables, container queries, and prefers-reduced-motion handling.Deliverables (explicit)- Output a complete project scaffold (files and code) ready to run with &#96;pnpm&#96;/&#96;npm&#96;:  - &#96;app/page.tsx&#96; (home)  - &#96;app/layout.tsx&#96; (meta, fonts, theme provider)  - &#96;components/*&#96; for each UI piece  - &#96;lib/data.ts&#96; or &#96;data/seed.ts&#96; with typed placeholder data  - &#96;public/&#96; with placeholder images (profile SVG) and &#96;resume.pdf&#96;  - &#96;styles/globals.css&#96; containing &#96;@import \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\";&#96; and your &#96;@theme&#96; declarations  - &#96;postcss.config.mjs&#96; referencing &#96;@tailwindcss/postcss&#96; if using PostCSS, or instructions to use &#96;@tailwindcss/vite&#96; for Vite users  - &#96;package.json&#96; with &#96;tailwindcss&#96; v4 and &#96;@tailwindcss/postcss&#96; / &#96;@tailwindcss/vite&#96; / &#96;@tailwindcss/cli&#96; as appropriate- Include a small README with run instructions and notes about where to plug the CMS later (which files to replace).- Keep code neat, well-commented, and idiomatic TypeScript/React.Important constraints (do not implement)- Do not build the CMS, user authentication, or live edit features now. Only create the static visuals and seed data.- Do not include external analytics or tracking scripts.- Do not use non-free or proprietary fonts; prefer Google Fonts or system fallbacks.Tone for copywriting- Confident, concise, and human. Provide short placeholder copy for name, tagline, project descriptions, and experience bullets that reads like a senior engineer (you can use realistic but fictional content).Final note- Make the bento grids a signature element — they should be visually distinct, memorable, and adaptable so the future CMS can change tile sizes/content. Prioritize a pristine mobile experience, while delivering an elegant and airy desktop layout.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n_**Agent (model claude-4.5-opus-high-thinking, mode Agent)**_\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"\u003c!-- Generated by SpecStory, Markdown v2.1.0 --\u003e\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":1},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":2},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"\u003c!-- cursor Session d136b2bd-7cc9-423b-94e6-d1e6f40e0054 (2025-12-01 10:48Z) --\u003e\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":3},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"# Static portfolio website design specifications (2025-12-01 10:48Z)\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":5},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":6},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"_**User (2025-12-01 08:24Z)**_\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":7},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":8},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Interprets this prompt that I am gonna use for v0 @Browser and divide it in paragraphs:\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":9},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":10},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":11},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":12},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Create a single, production-ready, static portfolio website (frontend only) for an elite software engineer.
